subject.title: RFC: policy on agent-directed instruction content in docs

question: Should ClawHub adopt a public acceptability rule for agent-directed instructions in SKILL.md/README content, and where should that rule live?
rationale: The issue defines a marketplace trust boundary rather than a broken current behavior, and current docs only cover adjacent unsafe execution and audit concepts.

options.title: Accept as policy work
options.body: Add concise allowed, needs-review, and not-allowed examples to public acceptable-use or publishing docs and mirror the security-review invariant in specs.

options.title: Fold into capability-manifest RFC
options.body: Resolve this boundary together with the declared-capability policy so manifest declarations and doc instructions share one trust model.

options.title: Keep internal for now
options.body: Leave agent-directed instruction judgment inside ClawScan/moderator review until maintainers are ready to publish a public rule.

recommendation.title: Accept as policy work
recommendation.body: Add concise allowed, needs-review, and not-allowed examples to public acceptable-use or publishing docs and mirror the security-review invariant in specs.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen is CODEOWNERS-listed and blame-backed for the relevant policy docs, RFC process, and ClawScan prompt surfaces.
